data.text:
From 6 - 12 January 2026, Two incidents of armed robbery against ships in Asia were reported to the ReCAAP ISC. 
 
⚓️ One incident occurred onboard a RoRo cargo ship while anchored at Batangas Anchorage, Philippines on 3 Jan 2026. The other incident occurred onboard a tug boat towing a barge in the eastbound lane of the Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS) in Singapore Strait (SS) on 5 Jan 2026.

🚨 The ReCAAP ISC advises ships to continue to intensify vigilance, maintain a sharp look-out while anchoring and transiting areas of concern, including the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, and report all incidents to the law enforcement agencies immediately; and the littoral States to increase patrols and enforcement in these areas.

Full report - https://t.co/2Z7QN2le2t

data.text:
Pull your seats.
A brief introduction summary into blue economy for deckhands, maintenance, ratings. 

These people are termed as 'Ratings.' Basically a non officer. Can be a deck rating, engine rating, Maintenance etc. These would provide tonnes of jobs for people we would refer to as wanabaharia (Sea goers). However, to go to sea on commercial vessels, you need an STCW certification. This gives you basic training on fire safety, drowning, accidents on board, MOB, personal survival etc. This is regardless of whether you are an officer or a rating, deckhand. Locally in Kenya, KMA (Kenya Maritime Authority) has this at Bandari College Mombasa. It's about 10 days. Used to be Ksh. 35,000 minus medical fees, seafarer book etc. Last year govt reduced it to Ksh. 15,000 still minus those other costs. This is also only available at Bandari so people from other counties will have to incur extra costs (Travel, meals, accommodation) for give or take 2 weeks).

When we launched the blue economy maneno, we had multiple arrangements with other countries and shipping lines on absorption  spearheaded by KMA (if anyone remembers the many interviews at Utalii almost every quarterly.)
Due to the Cost of training, Kenyans with a bit of means actually landed jobs in cruise ships. However for the hohehahe 40k for a few days is a lot of money and our agreements were mainly tailored to Intl cruise vessels so if you are a rating, they didn't need many of those. Indian ocean fishing boats would absorb an astronomical number of Kenyans. For now, Philippines and Dar are calling the shots on these I think at the moment. 

If we want to tap into the blue economy we have to think both Cruise international and 'domestic/Indian ocean Island vessels for the ratings people. 
We will also have to give the vessels ultimatums that 40-50% must be Kenyans if they are fishing in Kenyan waters. Not Filipinos. But our ministry of blue economy waziri katerina al Shisha is focused on selling mineral rights.
